responsibility: Implements GCC’s backend port for the IA-64/Itanium architecture, covering target-specific instruction selection, ABI rules, scheduling, and OS subtarget integration. The core files (`ia64.h`, `ia64.cc`/`ia64.c`, `ia64.md`, `ia64-modes.def`, and `ia64-protos.h`) define the architectural model, register-stack and calling-convention behavior, prologue/epilogue generation, asm and relocation hooks, builtin/atomic/vector helpers, and the main RTL patterns and attributes used for recognition, reload, bundling, and final emission. Companion machine-description fragments such as `constraints.md`, `predicates.md`, `div.md`, `sync.md`, `vect.md`, and `itanium2.md` refine operand legality, inline floating-point divide/sqrt sequences, atomic memory-model operations, packed/vector code generation, and Itanium 2 pipeline scheduling. The module also contains target option definitions (`ia64.opt`, `ilp32.opt`, `vms.opt`), front-end support for IA-64/HP-UX pragmas (`ia64-c.c`/`.cc`), intrinsic/header exposure, and multiple subtarget headers (`sysv4.h`, `linux.h`, `elf.h`, `freebsd.h`, `hpux*.h`, `vms.h`) that adapt the generic IA-64 backend to specific ABIs, runtimes, assemblers, linkers, and object-format conventions.
